why_partial: A required an eight-process U/Frequency/Front/Random/Random/Front/Frequency/U mirror. Integration failures consumed frozen A slots; all four strategies have one successful common-source block, but the second mirror is absent. Every candidate already failed the necessary W2 TPOT <=0.95 first-block gate, so Uniform remains selected, yet missing required coverage cannot be relabeled complete.

answers.static_placement: Uniform Q32 remains the appropriate static placement. Frequency, Front-loading and Random seed42 improved first-block W2 TPOT by only 3.01%, 0.78% and 3.11%, each below 5%, and introduced other workload regressions. Formal second mirror coverage is missing.
answers.remaining_hotspot: QSA Decode was the actionable remaining hotspot. Direct consumption of resident BF16 K/V rows removes redundant CPU staging while keeping vectorized Prefill and sparse-GQA math.
answers.deferred: Not worth device research under the frozen trigger: CPU Expert exposed wait was 6.7043% and 6.4842%, below 10%. No d=1 code ran, so Round13 did not change semantics and makes no deferred speed/quality claim.
answers.fresh_s0_gain: In F, W2 TPOT improved 32.23%/32.10%, E2E improved 29.81%/29.30%, and serial output throughput increased 41.65%/41.75%. Owned HBM was unchanged at 25,794 MiB; Host/whole-card peaks had no consistent paired regression.
